T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — regime stability, Iran's long-term resilience, durability of economic pressure campaign

**Synopsis:**
Six months into a US-Iran confrontation centered on the Strait of Hormuz, Washington is executing an intensified economic campaign — naval blockade plus historically tight sanctions — that is visibly straining Iran's economy (FX access, imports, fuel, wheat). Energy markets have adapted, limiting Iran's ability to inflict global economic shock. However, Tehran has not signaled meaningful concessions. Iran's Revolutionary Guards appear to be calibrating escalation rather than folding. A wartime patriotic mood is muting domestic unrest for now. Mediators are quietly exploring a face-saving formula around Hormuz shipping fees. The central question is whether Iran breaks before either side triggers another military confrontation.
